full_text:
Salim and his sister Salma were orphans of an honest merchant of Khorasan who grew up in mutual devotion, managing their family’s modest silk emporium. While traveling with a caravan to Baghdad, the caravan was scattered by desert brigands, and Salma was separated from her brother, carried away into captivity.

Salim swore never to rest until he had found his sister. He traversed deserts, worked as a caravan driver, and searched the markets of Syria and Iraq for three long years.

Meanwhile, Salma, through her extraordinary skill in calligraphy and arithmetic, had gained the respect of the Governor of Basra, who employed her as the chief ledger-keeper of the municipal granaries.

One afternoon, a weary caravan arrived at the granary, with Salim leading the pack-camels, covered in dust and in rags.

As he stepped before the accounting desk, Salma looked up: she recognized her brother’s voice!

She dropped her reed pen, ran from behind the lattice, and fell upon his neck with tears of boundless joy!

The Governor of Basra was deeply moved by their unbroken fraternal fidelity. He rewarded Salim with a merchant fleet, united them with their ancestral property, and celebrated their reunion, demonstrating that pure family love outlasts the darkest trials.
moral: Fraternal loyalty and courage bridge the widest deserts, reuniting family in joy. [ZH]
